learning_objectives: Elicit a focused chest-pain history using OPQRST
Identify cardiac risk factors and red-flag associated symptoms
Perform a relevant cardiovascular and respiratory exam
Communicate findings and next steps without alarming the patient

metadata.title: Chest Pressure After Walking From the Taxi Stand
metadata.chief_complaint: Tight, heavy pain in the middle of my chest for about 40 minutes.
metadata.setting: Emergency department, Samut Prakan — afternoon walk-in after driving a taxi shift

teaching_points: Gate radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, smoking, and family history until asked
Do not volunteer that the statin was stopped last month

disclosure_notes: Volunteer the crushing chest pressure and that it started while walking. Disclose radiation to the left arm, sweating, and nausea only if asked. Do not volunteer the family history of early MI or that you stopped your statin last month unless specifically asked. Never use terms like 'myocardial infarction' or 'ACS'.

patient_profile.living_situation: Lives with wife in a ground-floor apartment in Samut Prakan
patient_profile.demeanor: Anxious and slightly restless, cooperative but short of breath when speaking in long sentences. Wants reassurance that this is just indigestion.

language_style.speech_notes: Uses lay terms such as 'tightness like someone sitting on my chest' and 'sweating like I ran'. Speaks in short sentences. Avoids medical words.

clinical_history.chief_complaint: Tight, heavy pain in the middle of my chest for about 40 minutes.
clinical_history.history_of_present_illness: The pain started suddenly while I was walking from the taxi stand after lunch. It feels like a heavy pressure in the middle of my chest. I sat down but it has not gone away.

opqrst.onset: Sudden, about 40 minutes ago while walking after lunch
opqrst.provocation_palliation: Worse with walking; sitting and rest have not helped; no antacids taken
opqrst.quality: Crushing, heavy pressure, 'like an elephant sitting on my chest'
opqrst.region_radiation: Central chest, radiates to the left arm and jaw
opqrst.severity: 8 out of 10 at worst, now 7 out of 10
opqrst.time_course: Continuous since onset, no prior identical episodes; occasional 'indigestion' after heavy meals for 2 weeks

social_history.tobacco: Smokes 10 cigarettes per day for 25 years
social_history.diet_and_exercise: Irregular meals, mostly fried food; little exercise

family_history.notes: Patient describes it as 'a heart problem, he died suddenly'

review_of_systems_positives: Occasional ankle swelling at the end of long driving days

pe_findings.general: Middle-aged man sitting upright, diaphoretic, clutching the center of his chest, speaking in short phrases.

heent.head: Normocephalic, atraumatic, diaphoretic scalp
heent.eyes: No pallor or icterus; pupils equal and reactive
heent.neck: No JVD, no carotid bruits, trachea midline

respiratory.auscultation: Clear breath sounds, no crackles or wheeze
respiratory.work_of_breathing: Mildly increased, speaking in short sentences

cardiovascular.inspection: No chest wall deformity; mild diaphoresis
cardiovascular.palpation: No chest-wall tenderness; PMI not displaced
cardiovascular.auscultation: Tachycardic, regular; S1/S2 present; no murmur, rub, or gallop
cardiovascular.pulses: Radial pulses equal and regular; no radio-radial delay

neurologic.gait_or_coordination: Not assessed; patient remains seated due to pain

musculoskeletal.inspection: No chest wall deformity or rash
musculoskeletal.palpation: No reproducible chest-wall or costochondral tenderness
musculoskeletal.range_of_motion: Shoulders move freely without changing the chest pressure
musculoskeletal.special_tests: Chest-wall compression does not reproduce the pain

osce_checklist.station_title: Chest pain — history and focused exam

items.description: Introduces self, role, and confirms patient identity
Elicits OPQRST features of chest pain
items.scoring_notes: Must cover onset, quality, radiation, severity, and time course

items.description: Asks about diaphoresis, nausea, dyspnea, syncope
Explores cardiac risk factors (HTN, DM, smoking, family history, meds)
items.scoring_notes: Must ask about smoking and family history

items.description: Comments on distress, diaphoresis, and vital signs
Performs focused cardiovascular and respiratory exam
Explains concern and next steps in lay language
Recognizes possible acute coronary syndrome and urgency
items.scoring_notes: Does not need to name ACS to the patient

items.description: Maintains respect, consent, and draping throughout
